name: Open Wispr
tagline: A direct, lightweight speech-to-text alternative for Wspr-style dictation workflows.
notes: Highlighted as the Wspr-style open alternative. Keep source verification conservative until a stable release feed is published.

name: Whispur
tagline: Native transcription utility with local-first positioning and a clean Mac workflow.
notes: Useful comparison target for dictation alternatives; direct installer availability should be rechecked before featuring.

name: Wren
tagline: Small, privacy-minded AI dictation for macOS.
notes: Good fit for users who want dictation without a heavy subscription workflow.

name: whisper.cpp
tagline: Local Whisper inference for power users and scriptable transcription setups.
notes: Best for technical users who want local transcription building blocks rather than a polished app shell.

name: Rectangle
tagline: Keyboard-first window snapping and tiling.
notes: The default recommendation for Magnet-style snapping with no subscription.

name: AeroSpace
tagline: i3-inspired tiling window manager for macOS power users.
notes: For users who want deterministic tiling rather than floating-window nudges.

name: AltTab
tagline: Windows-style app and window switching for macOS.
notes: Strong replacement for commercial window switchers.

name: Ice
tagline: Modern open-source menu bar hiding and organization.
notes: The flagship open alternative after Bartender trust concerns.

name: Hidden Bar
tagline: Tiny menu bar item hider with a simple divider workflow.
notes: Good for users who want the simplest possible Bartender replacement.

name: Maccy
tagline: Fast clipboard history with keyboard-first search.
notes: The classic free replacement for subscription clipboard managers.

name: Quicksilver
tagline: Classic launcher and automation palette for keyboard-driven Mac users.
notes: A mature alternative for users who prefer classic launcher extensibility.

name: Hammerspoon
tagline: Lua automation bridge for windows, hotkeys, alerts, and system workflows.
notes: Excellent if you want programmable workflows instead of a paid macro suite.

name: Karabiner-Elements
tagline: Deep keyboard remapping and device-specific input customization.
notes: The reliable choice for complex keyboard remapping.

name: LinearMouse
tagline: Pointer acceleration, scrolling direction, and mouse tuning per device.
notes: A polished free replacement for commercial mouse-control utilities.

name: MonitorControl
tagline: Control external display brightness and volume from macOS.
notes: One of the strongest free utilities for external monitor control.

name: Stats
tagline: Menu bar system monitor for CPU, GPU, memory, network, sensors, and battery.
notes: Best-known open replacement for iStat-style menu bar telemetry.

name: KeepingYouAwake
tagline: Simple menu bar caffeine toggle to keep your Mac awake.
notes: A focused alternative for keeping a Mac awake without a complex rule engine.

name: Pearcleaner
tagline: Modern open-source app cleaner and leftover file remover.
notes: The best-looking modern open alternative to paid uninstallers.

name: AppCleaner
tagline: Classic app uninstaller that finds associated support files.
notes: A trusted lightweight option for app removal.

name: GrandPerspective
tagline: Disk usage treemap for finding large files and wasted space.
notes: A practical DaisyDisk-style visualization for free.

name: Keka
tagline: Fast file archiver and extractor with broad format support.
notes: A polished free alternative to paid archive managers.

name: OpenMTP
tagline: Android file transfer for macOS with a native two-pane interface.
notes: Useful replacement for paid Android transfer tools.

name: IINA
tagline: Modern macOS video player built on mpv.
notes: The obvious free replacement for many paid media players.

name: HandBrake
tagline: Video transcoder for converting media without paid converter suites.
notes: Gold-standard free video conversion.

name: Transmission
tagline: Clean BitTorrent client with a small footprint.
notes: A trusted free download client.

name: Cyberduck
tagline: FTP, SFTP, WebDAV, S3, and cloud storage file transfer.
notes: Longstanding open alternative to Transmit-style clients.

name: LocalSend
tagline: Cross-platform nearby file sharing without accounts or cloud relays.
notes: Great AirDrop-adjacent utility for mixed-device households.

name: Syncthing
tagline: Peer-to-peer file synchronization without a paid cloud subscription.
notes: Best fit when users want local control instead of cloud storage rent.

name: CotEditor
tagline: Native plain-text and code editor for macOS.
notes: A crisp native alternative to paid text editors.

name: Zed
tagline: Fast collaborative code editor from the Atom and Tree-sitter creators.
notes: Modern replacement for paid native developer editors.

name: Bruno
tagline: Offline-first API client with collection files stored in Git.
notes: Strong free alternative to Postman subscriptions.

name: Beekeeper Studio
tagline: Friendly SQL editor and database manager.
notes: Good option for teams that want a friendlier SQL client.

name: UTM
tagline: Virtual machines for macOS using QEMU and Apple virtualization.
notes: The best-known free Parallels alternative for Mac virtualization.

name: Colima
tagline: Container runtimes on macOS with minimal fuss.
notes: CLI-focused alternative for Docker Desktop and OrbStack workflows.

name: draw.io Desktop
tagline: Diagramming app for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, and docs.
notes: Solid free diagramming replacement for many paid visual tools.

name: Inkscape
tagline: Vector drawing and SVG editing.
notes: The standard free alternative to paid vector design apps.

name: GIMP
tagline: Image editing and raster graphics without an Adobe subscription.
notes: Best-known no-cost raster editor.

name: Krita
tagline: Digital painting and illustration studio.
notes: Strong free creative app for illustration and painting.

name: Blender
tagline: 3D modeling, animation, rendering, compositing, and video tools.
notes: The benchmark free alternative in 3D creation.

name: OBS Studio
tagline: Recording and live streaming with scenes, sources, and plugins.
notes: Powerful free alternative to paid screen recording suites.

name: Kap
tagline: Simple screen recorder for short captures and GIF-style workflows.
notes: Lightweight option for quick captures.

name: Audacity
tagline: Audio recording and editing for podcasts, cleanup, and simple production.
notes: Classic free audio editing option.

name: BlackHole
tagline: Virtual audio driver for routing sound between Mac apps.
notes: The free audio-routing building block many creators need.

name: LuLu
tagline: Outbound firewall that alerts when apps try to connect out.
notes: The best-known free Little Snitch alternative.

name: KnockKnock
tagline: Persistence scanner for startup items, launch agents, and suspicious components.
notes: Great utility for auditing what launches with your Mac.

name: OverSight
tagline: Alerts when the microphone or camera activates.
notes: Tiny privacy utility for mic/camera awareness.

name: SelfControl
tagline: Block distracting websites for a set period, even across restarts.
notes: A classic free focus blocker.

name: ActivityWatch
tagline: Local automatic time tracking and activity analytics.
notes: Free local alternative to paid time-tracking analytics.

name: Logseq
tagline: Local-first outlining, journaling, and linked notes.
notes: Strong free alternative to paid networked note tools.

name: Joplin
tagline: Markdown notes with end-to-end encrypted sync options.
notes: Great for users leaving subscription note apps.

name: Zettlr
tagline: Markdown writing, research, citations, and long-form notes.
notes: Better fit than generic notes apps for writers and academics.

name: MarkText
tagline: Distraction-free Markdown editor with live preview.
notes: A free Typora-style editor for Markdown writing.

name: AppFlowy
tagline: Open-source workspace for docs, tasks, tables, and knowledge.
notes: Good alternative for Notion-style workflows with more local control.

name: Ollama
tagline: Run local LLMs on macOS with a simple model pull workflow.
notes: Core local AI utility for Mac users who want models on device.

name: Jan
tagline: Open-source desktop app for running and chatting with local AI models.
notes: Friendly app layer for local model exploration.
